title: Power without purity will wreck what God is trying to build.
paragraphs: Power without purity will wreck what God is trying to build.

They cast out demons.
They prophesied.
They moved in power.

And still… Jesus said,
“I never knew you.” — Matthew 7:23
Let that sit.
You can be gifted… and still be lost.

You can lay hands on others
while secretly chained yourself.

You can speak fire on stage
but burn in private compromise.
That’s the danger.

Because spiritual gifts can impress people—
but only character pleases God.
And here’s where it cuts deep:

God never anointed your gift
to replace your obedience.
But here’s what we miss…

We chase the spotlight of gifting
and ignore the shadow work of character.

We want the microphone
but not the pruning.

We want influence
without surrender.
Yet Scripture is clear:
“The gifts and calling of God are irrevocable.” — Romans 11:29
Meaning?

God may still use your gift…
even while your character is cracking.

Not because He approves—
but because He’s merciful to the people you’re reaching.
But don’t confuse usefulness with intimacy.

Judas had power.
He walked with Jesus.
He witnessed miracles.
And still betrayed Him. — Luke 22:48
And that’s where grace walks in.

Not to excuse the gap—
but to close it.

Jesus didn’t die just to make you powerful.
He died to make you pure.

Not just anointed—
but transformed.

Because the real evidence of the Spirit
is not just what flows through you…
…but what has been crucified within you. — Galatians 5:24

So if your gift is growing
but your character is shrinking…
Don’t ignore that.
Run back to the cross.

Repent quickly.
Surrender deeply.
Let God rebuild the foundation—
before the platform collapses.

You don’t need more gifting.
You need more of Christ.
And the beautiful truth?

He’s not waiting to expose you—
He’s waiting to restore you.
